The International Vaccine Institute (IVI) has paid tribute to renowned Ghanaian malaria researcher and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS), Professor Fred Newton Binka, following his death at age 73.
In a Facebook post on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the Institute described Prof. Binka as a pioneering malaria researcher and dedicated educator whose work contributed significantly to infectious disease prevention and public health development in Ghana and beyond.
The Institute also acknowledged his role in training successive generations of scientists and health professionals during his tenure as the founding Vice-Chancellor of UHAS.
"IVI mourns the passing of Professor Fred Newton Binka, a pioneering malaria researcher, dedicated educator, and former member of IVI’s Board of Trustees," the post stated.
Prof. Binka served on IVI's Board of Trustees from 2014 to 2020, contributing to the Institute's work in advancing vaccine research and improving global health.
The Institute expressed gratitude for his leadership and extended its condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, students and others whose lives he influenced.
"We are grateful for his leadership and extend our heartfelt condolences to Prof. Binka’s family, friends, colleagues, students, and all those whose lives he touched," it added.
Prof. Binka was a leading figure in Ghana's public health sector, having served as the founding Vice-Chancellor of UHAS when the institution was established in March 2012.

Before his appointment, he was Dean of the School of Public Health at the University of Ghana, Legon, and spent more than two decades working with the Ministry of Health.
During his career, he established the Navrongo Health Research Centre, which gained international recognition for its contribution to health research, and founded the INDEPTH Network, comprising 33 research sites across 24 developing countries in Africa and Asia.
He also served on more than a dozen World Health Organisation expert committees and panels and chaired the GAVI Independent Review Committee.
In recognition of his contribution to UHAS, the university named its School of Public Health after him in June 2022.
His work in malaria research earned him several international honours, including the inaugural Rudolf Geigy Award in 2001 and the Ronald Ross Medal from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in 2010.
Until his death, Prof. Binka was the Chairman of the Governing Council of the Ghana Health Service.
